newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares open higher, outlook seen firm.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares open higher, outlook seen firm.

text.p: Singapore stock prices broke through the 2,200 barrier in early trade on Thursday and could continue to rise into next week on momentum from Wall Street, dealers said.
"The rise will last for the rest of this week and possibly into the early part of next," one international dealer said.
The benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index stood at 2,204.50, up 10.22 points, at 0217 GMT.
Early morning trade saw 165 gainers against 43 losers on volume of 44.43 million shares at 0217 GMT, with blue chips inching steadily up, dealers said.
But a fairly flat end to the year was expected by dealers who were cautious about where and when the index would plateau.
"Manufacturers are still seeing slow order books, so confidence is not yet reflected in Singapore's general economic performance," the dealer said.
"Singapore will become much more interesting in the early part of next year to foreign investors as the expected recovery begins," said another.
The concensus is that Singapore shares will continue to move up, said dealers, but it is too early to make accurate forecasts of the growth range.
